Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Virtually every outlet is dominated by the dramatic reversal in AI/tech stocks following the Democrats' sweeping midterm wins, with investors suddenly worried that newly elected officials who campaigned against data centers will slow the AI buildout. Secondary threads include fallout from a Paraguay banking scandal that toppled a president, hedge funds unwinding crowded AI bets, and a string of corporate breakup/takeover stories (CVS, Wendy's).

stories.headline: AI-driven stock rout wipes out trillions after Democratic midterm sweep
stories.summary: U.S. stocks suffered their worst day in over a year as Nasdaq fell into correction territory, erasing a post-election rally, after Democrats' midterm wins raised fears of tougher scrutiny on AI data centers; losses then spread to Asian and European markets.

stories.headline: Voters nationwide approve dozens of measures to restrict AI data centers
stories.summary: Axios reports that roughly two dozen of 41 ballot measures across 10 states passed restrictions on data centers, with Democrats sweeping governorships in Texas, Ohio, Georgia and Arizona—the top states for planned AI capacity—signaling a political backlash against the AI buildout.

stories.headline: OpenAI overhauls data-center practices after election rebuke
stories.summary: OpenAI pledged to drop nondisclosure agreements and shield residents from footing electricity bills for its data centers, a policy shift announced just two days after voters backed candidates pushing for AI curbs.

stories.headline: Paraguay's president resigns as bank collapse tied to him sparks crisis
stories.summary: Santiago Peña stepped down after the collapse of a bank with close ties to him shook a South American economy that had drawn heavy investor interest and built close ties with Washington.

stories.headline: Hedge funds dump AI-linked positions and cut staff as selloff deepens
stories.summary: Stock-picking hedge funds unwound positions last month at the fastest pace in more than a decade as the AI trade soured, with Bloomberg separately noting crowded trades unraveling rapidly after a rough October.

stories.headline: Investors skeptical Anthropic can justify $1.5 trillion IPO valuation
stories.summary: Major investors are doubting Anthropic can hit a $1.5 trillion valuation in its planned IPO, though some believe strong October financial results could soften the blow of the broader market rout.

stories.headline: CVS Health moves to split itself up
stories.summary: CVS Health is planning a breakup, with analysts saying its retail pharmacy and other units may now be strong enough to stand alone after a roughly two-year turnaround; The Economist calls the move a turning point for vertically integrated U.S. health care.

stories.headline: Wendy's rejects $1.4 billion takeover bid from Nelson Peltz's Trian
stories.summary: Wendy's turned down a $1.4 billion takeover proposal from Trian, saying the offer undervalues potential gains from the burger chain's turnaround strategy.

Business.gaps: Puck, The Information, Forbes, Puck and Politico produced little distinct business-specific coverage beyond the shared AI-selloff/midterms story already captured; Business Insider could not be checked via search and had no relevant feed items.

US politics.overview: Coverage across nearly every US politics outlet is dominated by the fallout from Tuesday's midterm elections, in which Democrats won sweeping control of the House, Senate, and a majority of governorships and state legislatures. Secondary threads include a bitter GOP recriminations fight over 2028 (Vance, DeSantis, Cruz), the legal battle over Trump's planned Arlington triumphal arch, and early market jitters tied to the political shake-up.

stories.headline: Democrats sweep midterms, flip House and Senate in historic rout
stories.summary: Democrats seized both chambers of Congress and made inroads deep into red territory including Texas, Georgia and South Carolina, in what Axios calls one of the most sweeping repudiations of a sitting president in modern history. Multiple outlets covered the scale of the rout, including record Senate pickups and a potential 255-seat House majority.

stories.headline: GOP erupts in recrimination as Vance, DeSantis and Cruz jockey for 2028
stories.summary: Vice President Vance is drawing criticism for blaming the Iran war and Israel for the GOP's midterm wipeout, while DeSantis and Cruz are positioning themselves as early frontrunners for the 2028 Republican nomination. Fox News, Washington Examiner, The Dispatch and National Review all ran parallel pieces on Vance privately faulting Netanyahu and the party's fractured post-mortem.

stories.headline: Judge blocks Trump's Arlington triumphal arch hours after federal approval
stories.summary: The National Capital Planning Commission approved Trump's long-championed arch between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery, but a federal judge issued a restraining order blocking construction just after midnight. The Hill and Fox News also covered the rapid approval-then-injunction sequence.

stories.headline: Democrats shatter GOP's 16-year hold on state legislatures
stories.summary: Democrats are on track to flip 12 legislative chambers, dismantle five Republican trifectas and build new supermajorities, giving them control over policy on minimum wage, abortion and voting rules heading into 2028. Stateline's series detailed parallel results on ballot measures covering abortion, trans sports bans, taxes and noncitizen voting.

stories.headline: House Republicans divided over leadership after devastating losses, NRCC chair ousted
stories.summary: House Republicans are split between those pushing for a leadership overhaul and others defending the current team, while NRCC Chairman Richard Hudson — tasked with protecting the majority — lost his own North Carolina seat. Roll Call and Axios also flagged Hudson's defeat as a symbolically brutal element of the rout.

stories.headline: Youth, Latino and Black voters swung hard to Democrats
stories.summary: Young voters, including Gen Z men who had drifted toward Trump in 2024, broke hard for Democrats this cycle, part of a broader realignment that also saw Latino voters in Texas and Black voters nationally swing back toward the party. Axios and NPR published detailed demographic breakdowns showing similar swings among Black and Hispanic voters.

stories.headline: SCOTUS weighs midterm fallout and hears new term's cases
stories.summary: SCOTUSblog examined how the midterm results could shape the Supreme Court's docket, alongside its ongoing term covering habeas procedure, pretrial firing disputes, and federal officials' liability for constitutional violations.

stories.headline: Global markets slide on AI slowdown fears after Democratic sweep
stories.summary: Asian and European markets tumbled, with London's FTSE down 1.9%, following a rout in US tech stocks as investors reassess AI spending bets in light of the midterm power shift. WSJ similarly examined what the midterm shake-up means for markets and investors.

US politics.gaps: No recent politics-specific coverage could be found for NOTUS; Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian items are limited to the feed provided since those outlets block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and business outlets this week is dominated by the fallout from Tuesday's US midterms, where Democratic wins and a wave of local anti-data-center ballot measures triggered a sharp selloff in AI stocks and renewed scrutiny of the industry's infrastructure bets. Alongside that, outlets are tracking Anthropic's wobbling $1.5 trillion IPO, OpenAI's new offensive cybersecurity model, and a fresh round of consolidation and policy fights involving Tesla, Meta, Google, TikTok and the New York Times.

stories.headline: AI stock rout and data-center backlash roil markets after Democratic midterm sweep
stories.summary: Global markets have been shaken as investors worry that newly elected Democratic governors who campaigned on pausing or halting data-center construction will slow the AI buildout, with Bloomberg noting that roughly 40% of planned U.S. data-center capacity sits in states where incoming governors have pledged to curb projects. The Information reports that executives and investors now fear delays in bringing new computing capacity online will make existing AI servers more expensive to run, while 404 Media found that data-center measures lost in most of the dozens of races where they appeared on the ballot.

stories.headline: Anthropic's $1.5 trillion IPO hits investor resistance amid market rout
stories.summary: Anthropic's planned IPO is running into trouble as investors push back on its targeted $1.5 trillion valuation just as the broader tech market sells off; The Register separately reports the company's own S-1 filing warns its blistering 12x revenue growth rate is unlikely to continue even as compute commitments near $900 billion.

stories.headline: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production in 2027 to boost Cybercab output
stories.summary: Elon Musk said Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck in 2027 and use the Texas Gigafactory space to ramp up production of its Cybercab robotaxi, a move Techmeme notes Musk framed as making room "to make room for increased Cybercab production."

stories.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, an AI model that finds and patches software vulnerabilities
stories.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized model built to find exploitable vulnerabilities and develop fixes while staying within authorized scope; VentureBeat reports the model's API pricing of $20 per million input tokens and $100 per million output tokens puts it above both its predecessor and rival offerings from Anthropic and Google.

stories.headline: Meta, Google and TikTok sue California AG over teen social media law
stories.summary: The three platforms are challenging a California law set to take effect next year that would restrict social media access for children under 16.

stories.headline: New York Times reportedly in talks to buy Letterboxd for $330 million
stories.summary: The Times Company is said to be in exclusive negotiations to acquire the fast-growing film-lovers' social network Letterboxd for around $330 million.

stories.headline: Democrats eye Apple, Meta and Musk companies as early congressional investigation targets
stories.summary: After winning House and Senate majorities, Democrats are reportedly laying groundwork to investigate major tech companies including Apple, Meta and Elon Musk-led firms once they take control of Congress.

stories.headline: Rare strike in Taiwan exposes labor unrest beneath the global AI chip rush
stories.summary: Workers at a Micron facility in Taoyuan protested outside the Micron facility demanding a greater share of profits and better bonuses, highlighting tensions between labor and the AI-driven chip boom.

Tech & AI.gaps: Google DeepMind had no company announcements in the allowed window; Platformer's most recent coverage (a column on the AI backlash and Democrats' plans) was over 24 hours old relative to other items but is included for context since no newer post was found.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by fallout from this week's US midterm elections and what the wave of Democratic wins means for utility regulation, data-center buildout, and permitting reform. Secondary threads include the start of COP31 in Antalya, a sharp oil price drop as Middle East war-risk premiums unwind, and new climate data on a developing 'super El Niño' and falling Chinese emissions.

stories.headline: Midterm Wins Reshape Democrats' Energy and Climate Strategy
stories.summary: Heatmap argues Democrats' midterm sweep signals a new, more moderate era of energy politics, with winning candidates downplaying climate ambition in favor of affordability and 'all of the above' energy messaging while still backing clean energy tax credits and transmission. A companion piece, 'The Anti-Utility Election,' notes utilities emerged as a top target in candidates' platforms, and another covers Democrats flipping two seats on Arizona's utility commission.

stories.headline: Voters' Backlash Against Data Centers and Utilities Shapes Policy Outlook
stories.summary: Latitude Media's post-election coverage argues voters delivered a clear anti-data-center message and that Democratic governors who ran on 'ratepayer defense' will now have to translate that into policy, while a separate piece notes a FERC commissioner saying regulators should embrace distributed energy resources after the 'blue wave.'

stories.headline: Democrats' State Wins Open Door for Clean Energy Push
stories.summary: Canary Media reports that Democratic victories in governor's races and statehouses could let party officials push utilities and data centers toward cleaner energy and lower costs, part of a broader roundup on what the election results mean for clean energy.

stories.headline: COP31 Opens in Antalya With Push for Global Electrification Target
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that negotiators at next week's COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey, are aiming for a voluntary commitment to lift the global share of final energy demand from electricity to 35% by 2035, though consensus remains uncertain. Carbon Brief is separately tracking the summit's draft negotiating texts and a Brazil-led 'roadmap' on deforestation and fossil-fuel transition released ahead of the talks.

stories.headline: Oil Slides Below $100 as War-Risk Bets Unwind
stories.summary: Bloomberg says oil's drop below $100 reflects traders unwinding bets on conflict escalation, but cautions that lasting peace — and market calm — is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: 'Super El Niño' on Track to Peak in December
stories.summary: Carbon Brief reports the rapidly developing 'super El Niño' is expected to peak at the end of 2026, pushing average global temperatures higher.

stories.headline: China's Quarterly CO2 Emissions Post Largest Drop Since Covid
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's analysis finds China's CO2 emissions fell 3.1% in the third quarter of 2026, the steepest quarterly drop since the pandemic, coinciding with the Hormuz crisis.

stories.headline: Rhodium Analysis: Bipartisan Permitting Bill Would Likely Cut Emissions
stories.summary: A new Rhodium Group analysis shared with Heatmap finds the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act would likely modestly cut US emissions and lower electricity bills by 2040, and would not increase emissions even in a worst-case scenario, though the bill's prospects have dimmed somewhat since the midterms.

Energy.gaps: E&E News' site now mostly redirects to Politico Pro coverage with no fresh stand-alone articles found in the last 48 hours; Argus Media had no retrievable recent coverage; The Economist, FT, and WSJ block search and had no relevant items in the provided feed.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage clusters around market turmoil triggered by the global AI stock selloff hitting Taiwan hardest, Beijing's intensifying efforts to prop up Chinese equities and the yuan, and a fresh wave of national-security prosecutions in Hong Kong and Macau. Tech-focused outlets are also tracking a flurry of Chinese AI model launches and the US-China tech/trade truce extension.

stories.headline: Taiwan's Taiex suffers historic plunge, stabilization fund steps in
stories.summary: Taiwan's benchmark index tumbled over 4.5% to its fourth-largest single-day point loss as the global AI stock rout deepened after the US midterms, prompting the National Financial Stabilization Fund to authorize market intervention.

stories.headline: Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in Hong Kong national security case
stories.summary: Jailed pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong received a 10-year sentence after pleading guilty to colluding with foreign forces, drawing praise from Hong Kong officials and condemnation from foreign governments and rights groups.

stories.headline: Beijing escalates stock-market rescue measures as yuan surges
stories.summary: China's central bank cut its stock buyback relending rate to 1% after banks sought over 200 billion yuan in quotas, part of a broader push including a third swap-facility operation and a forex reserve requirement hike to curb the yuan's rally, all aimed at restoring investor confidence after a sharp market downturn.

stories.headline: China's indebted tycoons weigh on the banking system
stories.summary: An Economist analysis examines how Chinese lenders are still absorbing losses from a decade of aggressive, debt-fueled expansion by private tycoons.

stories.headline: Apple's China AI partnership with Alibaba's Qwen begins rocky rollout
stories.summary: Apple Intelligence began beta testing in China on November 4 with Alibaba's Qwen model powering select Siri and Visual Intelligence features, a partnership the outlet says has faced a turbulent path.

stories.headline: Taiwan chip workers' strike highlights labor tension in the AI boom
stories.summary: A rare strike by Micron Technology union workers in Taoyuan, demanding bigger profit shares and bonuses, is spotlighting growing labor unrest beneath the region's AI-driven growth.

stories.headline: Macau sentences ex-lawmaker Au Kam San to 12.5 years in first national security trial
stories.summary: A Macau court sentenced former democracy campaigner and ex-lawmaker Au Kam San to 12 years and six months for subversion and other offences, marking the territory's first national security trial.

China.gaps: CGTN, Yicai Global and Sixth Tone yielded no distinct recent China-politics/economy coverage in search results; Global Times and China Daily results were mostly older or generic items rather than fresh 24-48h leads. Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and WSJ block search and had no feed items provided, so their current coverage could not be assessed.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets remains dominated by the fragile Iran-US standoff following the US midterms, with intense diplomatic activity via Qatar alongside continued Houthi-Saudi missile exchanges. A second major thread is the fraying US-Israel relationship and stalled Saudi normalization prospects, while regional business outlets flag economic strains from the war alongside new Gulf infrastructure and investment moves.

stories.headline: Iran sends nuclear proposal to US via Qatar as Trump weighs new strikes
stories.summary: Tehran has submitted a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatari mediators, but insists it will only be discussed once the US meets seven Iranian demands including lifting sanctions and paying war reparations, while Trump says he is weighing whether to resume strikes.

stories.headline: Saudi coalition intercepts fresh wave of Houthi missiles and drones
stories.summary: Saudi air defences intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at Najran and a drone over Mecca on Friday, part of an intensifying barrage that also targeted the Madinah region earlier in the week.

stories.headline: Israel's US alliance frays as Saudi normalization ruled out under Netanyahu
stories.summary: A week after Israel's inconclusive election, Americans delivered Congress to Democrats pushing a tougher line on Israel over Iran, Gaza and the West Bank, while a Saudi source told Israeli media normalization "is not on the agenda" while Netanyahu remains in power.

stories.headline: Kurdish party PUK withdraws from Kurdistan Regional Government
stories.summary: The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan, led by the Talabani family, has pulled out of the KRG, a rupture that could unravel the semi-autonomous Iraqi region recognized under the 2005 constitution.

stories.headline: Bahrain says landmark GCC railway deal to be signed November 8
stories.summary: Bahrain has announced that a long-awaited agreement linking GCC countries by rail will be signed on November 8, a project seen as key to regional connectivity and supply-chain resilience.

stories.headline: Gulf AI bets face scrutiny after US tech sell-off
stories.summary: A sharp sell-off in US tech stocks is raising questions about returns on the tens of billions of dollars Gulf sovereign funds have poured into AI infrastructure, with analysts warning fiscal and energy pressures from the Iran war compound the risk.

stories.headline: Displaced mothers in Yemen's besieged Taiz scavenge plastic to survive
stories.summary: Two single mothers who fled their village three weeks ago described struggling to keep their children fed and warm amid the siege of Taiz, as air strikes on a local market reportedly killed or wounded more than 30 people.

stories.headline: Gaza ceasefire violence continues as aid restrictions hit burn patients
stories.summary: MSF says it may halt production of 3D-printed masks for burn victims because Israel is blocking materials deemed dual-use, as strikes and gunfire killed five more Palestinians in Gaza despite the ongoing truce.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not access Saudi Gazette, Zawya, Arabian Business, Ynetnews, or Iran International beyond general homepage/trending content; no outlet-specific recent lead story was confirmed for these titles in the search window.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage is converging on Tanzania's climactic Lissu treason verdict and South Africa's local elections, while business-focused outlets are tracking Nigeria's Dangote refinery IPO, Washington's AGOA exclusions of South Africa and Rwanda, and Nigeria's new crypto and stablecoin regulations. African Business and Africa Confidential are also flagging the fallout from US trade and sanctions pressure on Pretoria and Kigali, alongside routine mining-sector earnings.

stories.headline: Tanzania court jails opposition leader Tundu Lissu for incitement, drops treason charge
stories.summary: After 19 months in detention, Tanzania's main opposition leader was convicted of incitement but spared the treason charge that could have carried a death sentence, ending a trial that drew international scrutiny.

stories.headline: ANC continues decline in South Africa's local elections
stories.summary: Support for the African National Congress kept falling in South Africa's municipal elections, though the party remains the largest and some leaders hope for a comeback modeled on Brazil's Lula; African Business separately reported the ANC was on track for its worst-ever municipal result with half the votes counted.

stories.headline: US strips South Africa and Rwanda of AGOA trade benefits
stories.summary: The Trump administration has removed South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act, citing rule-of-law and security concerns, with South Africa's AGOA exports already down from $4bn in 2024 to near $1.5bn in 2025, and Rwanda's exclusion following US sanctions over its backing of M23 rebels in Congo.

stories.headline: Dangote Refinery's $1.6bn IPO draws almost triple demand
stories.summary: Nigerian investors placed roughly $4.78bn in orders for Dangote Refinery's planned November listing, underscoring strong domestic appetite as the $1.6bn offering closed oversubscribed.

stories.headline: Namibia's president takes personal charge of Dangote's $2.5bn fuel project
stories.summary: President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah says she will personally oversee Dangote's fuel storage and regional pipeline investment, breaking her own rule to avoid bureaucratic delays costing Namibia another major project.

stories.headline: Nigeria's central bank overhauls crypto and stablecoin oversight
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria is tightening its grip on digital assets, introducing a $744,000 capital rule splitting oversight with the securities regulator, a new requirement linking peer-to-peer crypto payments to bank transactions, and an $11.16 million capital threshold for foreign stablecoin issuers.

stories.headline: Guinea-Bissau cancels US-funded hepatitis B vaccine trial on newborns
stories.summary: After weeks of controversy, Guinea-Bissau scrapped a proposed hepatitis B vaccine trial on newborns following mounting criticism that it was unethical and exploitative.

stories.headline: Russia's arms market in Africa slips as Putin pushes $20bn offensive
stories.summary: Once Africa's dominant arms supplier, Moscow has fallen behind the US and China, prompting a renewed sales push including fighter jets and air-defence systems at the third Russia-Africa Summit.

Africa.gaps: The Continent's site returned only older archived issues with no stories from the last 48 hours. Mining Weekly's recent output was dominated by routine quarterly earnings and project updates (AngloGold, Sibanye-Stillwater, Caledonia) rather than major newsworthy developments. Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block direct search and no relevant feed items were supplied for them in this cycle.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past 48 hours is dominated by two threads: the fallout and ratings bonanza from the U.S. midterms (how networks and newsletters covered election night and its aftermath), and a wave of corporate/financial news in media — The New York Times' subscriber growth, USA Today Co.'s AI-linked losses, Meta's regulatory and policy moves, and Trump Media's shaky finances. Hollywood trade press is separately focused on the Russell Brand trial fallout and Pamela Abdy's blistering speech on the industry's treatment of women.

stories.headline: New York Times boosts digital subscribers by 420,000 in three months
stories.summary: The New York Times added 420,000 new digital subscribers in the third quarter of 2026, keeping it on track to hit its goal of 15 million subscriptions by the end of 2027.

stories.headline: Steve Kornacki and NBC drew crowds as midterms got a ratings bump
stories.summary: More than 31 million viewers tuned in for coverage of the Democrats' big midterm night, a 23 percent jump over the 2022 midterms, as cable and broadcast networks battled for ratings supremacy on election night.

stories.headline: Meta, Google and TikTok sue to block California law protecting minors on social media
stories.summary: The three tech giants are suing to stop a California law, set to take effect in 2027, that would prohibit addictive feeds, endless scrolling and autoplayed video for users under 16.

stories.headline: Meta pulls down controversial terms of service
stories.summary: Meta has indefinitely delayed proposed commercial terms of service that would have let it scrape the websites of Meta Business account users, after backlash from publishers.

stories.headline: Russell Brand trial fallout spreads through British media and entertainment
stories.summary: In the wake of Russell Brand's rape and sexual assault conviction, a British comedy producer accused of laughing during one assault has been dropped from BBC and Apple shows, prosecutors agreed to omit mention of his marriage to Katy Perry, and Bear Grylls — who baptized Brand — said "justice has now been served."

stories.headline: Pamela Abdy unloads on Hollywood's treatment of women in WIF Honors speech
stories.summary: The former Warner Bros. film chief delivered a fiery speech at the Women in Film Honors criticizing Hollywood's support networks for male directors compared to women, while also saying she has "no idea" what she's doing next after her Warner exit.

stories.headline: USA Today Co. blames AI for its revenue woes while also betting on AI as a fix
stories.summary: USA Today Co., the country's largest newspaper chain, reported a weak third quarter including a net loss and declining revenue, pointing partly to AI-driven disruption even as it leans on AI tools as part of its turnaround plan.

stories.headline: Trump Media shifts $342M in Bitcoin as $1B debt deadline looms
stories.summary: Trump's media company transferred roughly $342 million in Bitcoin to a crypto exchange, raising questions about a possible sell-off weeks before a potential $1 billion debt repayment deadline on its convertible notes.

Media.gaps: Status, WSJ, FT and The Guardian had no retrievable recent media-industry coverage in this window; Status's own site returned only older archival pages rather than current-day items, and WSJ/FT/Guardian block search so only feed items (none provided for them) could be used.
